h: The Third Meal Teaches Dependence on Divine Help

p: Regarding the night it is stated (Pesachim 106a):
And likewise by day the Sages instituted
which is not so at the third meal.
And likewise in the Gemara (Berachos 42b) it is stated:
הוֹאִיל וְאָדָם קוֹבֵעַ סְעוּדָתוֹ עַל הַיַּיִן
since a person establishes his meal over wine";
and nevertheless we have not seen
that they instituted Kiddush over wine
only at night and in the morning;
wine has no connection to this meal.
as the Ari, of blessed memory, arranged them:
corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom;
corresponds to Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom;
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom.
And with Yitzchak we find explicitly (Bereishis 27:25):
"And he brought him wine and he drank";
and likewise with Avraham we find (21:8):
"And Yaakov offered a sacrifice on the mountain
and called his kinsmen to eat bread,"
which is only meat and bread;
"And wine gladdens the heart (levav) of man,"
for it gladdens the two hearts,
the heart of the wise and the heart of the fool;
for wine can bring a joy
עֲרָיוֹת כּוּלָּן דּוֹמוֹת עָלָיו כְּמִישׁוֹר כוּ׳
"All forbidden relations seem to him like a level plain, etc.;
seems to him like a level plain," etc.
וְהִנֵּה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר
Now Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom, said (Bereishis 48:15):
"The God before whom my fathers walked,"
that is, each one served with his own trait:
Avraham with the trait of love of Hashem Yisbarach,
and Yitzchak with the trait of fear,
for Hashem Yisbarach stood before him
"The God who has shepherded me, etc.,"
that Hashem Yisbarach alone leads him,
and he himself does not sense at all
that he accomplishes anything through his service.
My help is from Hashem, etc.":
לֵית אַנְתְּ מוֹבֵיד סִבְרִי מִן בְּרִיִּי
"Will you not abandon your hope in My creatures?"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּצֵא)
(as stated in Bereishis Rabbah, beginning of Vayetze).
that there did not avail him
the teaching of his masters and his fathers,
as they said, "to teach me and to delight me."
"And one who wishes to become wealthy should face north";
and we said that it means:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as King Shlomo, alav hashalom, said (Mishlei 30:8-9):
lest I be sated and deny"
that is, hold fast to the trait of fear,
מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
the trait of Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom,
and then wealth will not harm him.
'In all toil there is profit' is written;
That is, when the yoke of tefillin is upon him,
which is the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven,
and Hashem Yisbarach stands before his eyes,
then the joy will not harm him.
הָלוֹךְ וְגָדוֹל עַד כִּי גָדַל מְאֹד
"growing ever greater until he was very great,"
"the dung of his mules," etc. (Bereishis Rabbah 64:7);
and likewise it is written of him:
"And he brought him wine and he drank"
that the wealth or the wine would harm him.
And with Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
it was on the day Yitzchak was weaned,
for a son was born to him
and was circumcised on the eighth day;
and he knew that he was already bound to the root,
for he was circumcised on the eighth, without his own awareness,
that is, he was born in holiness.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי הִתִּיר לוֹ אָז הַיַּיִן
And therefore he then permitted himself wine;
and it is written "a great feast,"
and it is stated in Midrash Rabbah (Bereishis Rabbah 53:10):
"The Great One of the worlds was there";
for he already knew that he was bound to the root, in Atika;
and even though he had not yet merited
what is said, "And Avraham was old,"
he knew then that he was bound to the root.
who said, "The God who has shepherded me all my life,"
that his help is only from Hashem,
lest he be corrupted, Heaven forbid.
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר
And likewise King David, alav hashalom, said (Divrei HaYamim I 22:14):
and it is stated (in the Yerushalmi, Pe'ah, chapter 4)
וְהוּא שֶׁאָמַר ה׳ רוֹעִי (תְּהִלִּים כג, א)
and he is the one who said "Hashem is my shepherd" (Tehillim 23:1),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom, said,
"The God who has shepherded me, etc.";
so that the eating not corrupt him.
And therefore at the third meal,
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
there is no connection to wine,
"Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack."

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וְהוּא שֶׁאָמַר ה׳ רוֹעִי (תְּהִלִּים כג, א)

paragraphs.text: Source: Tehillim 23:1 — “מזמור לדוד יהוה רעי לא אחסר” — “A psalm of David. GOD is my shepherd; I lack nothing.”
